prompt: Priya posted an alert about OOM kills hitting the cluster-b inference pods in one of our channels. For the incident postmortem, pull the member list — with each person's workspace role — for whichever workspace contains that channel.
binding_note: The route is workspace_membership -> workspace -> conversation -> message -> user. Priya authoring the cluster-b/OOM alert message pins the conversation (#core-infra, C_INFRA) and, through its team_id, pins the workspace (T01WORKSPACE) rather than the similarly-themed Orbit Labs workspace where a different person posted about an OOM issue in a different channel. The deliverable is the set of workspace_membership rows (stored as user_teams) belonging to that pinned workspace, each carrying its own role attribute.

roles.reason: Anchors the identifying chain to one conversation via its author.

roles.facts: T01WORKSPACE ('Test Workspace'), the workspace owning C_INFRA.
roles.reason: The workspace resolved by the route, whose memberships are the deliverable.

obligations.name: pinned_workspace_membership_roster
obligations.description: Select all user_teams (workspace_membership) rows belonging to the workspace that owns the conversation containing the message where Priya reported the cluster-b/OOM alert; report each member's user and role.
obligations.scope: ordinary requested scope: every workspace_membership row for the single workspace resolved via the message-authorship route

task_spec.text: Find the channel containing Priya's cluster-b/OOM memory-pressure alert message, determine which workspace it belongs to, and list that workspace's members together with their workspace roles.

access_plan: Use conversations.list/conversations.history (or search.messages with a query like 'OOM cluster-b') to locate the alert message and confirm its author is Priya and its channel is core-infra; use conversations.info on that channel to obtain its team_id (T01WORKSPACE). Then call users.list scoped with team_id=T01WORKSPACE to enumerate the workspace's members and their roles, which corresponds to the user_teams rows for that team.
